chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Which type of Hajj is the most superior?' He said, 'Al-Tamattu'. And how can anything be superior to it, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says, 'If I had anticipated from my affair what I encountered later, I would have done as the people did.'

key_terms.اَلتَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior type of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Hajj al-Tamattu' as the most virtuous form, citing the Prophet’s statement that had he foreseen his later hardships, he would have performed Hajj like the general populace. Shia scholars interpret this as the Prophet preferring the communal, easier practice of Tamattu' (or Qiran) over his unique, more rigorous Hajj al-Ifrad, highlighting the merit of following the collective tradition. This narration underscores the flexibility and spiritual reward of Tamattu' in Shia jurisprudence, where the pilgrist performs Umrah and Hajj separately with a break in between.
